Tracking the Status of Your Ballot 
Current Availability 
Absentee ballots for the 2026 General Election are now available at the Lebanon City Clerk's Office.  
About Absentee Voting 
New Hampshire does not offer general early voting. However, qualified voters may vote by absentee if they are unable to vote in person on Election Day because of:  
Absence from Lebanon 
Religious observance 
Disability 
Employment obligations, including caring for children or infirm adults 
Confinement in a penal institution for a misdemeanor or while awaiting trial 
Each election requires a separate absentee ballot application. 
Severe Weather 
If the National Weather Service issues a winter storm, blizzard, or ice storm warning for Election Day, certain voters may qualify to vote absentee on the Monday immediately before the election, including: 
Elderly, infirm, or disabled voters concerned about safely traveling in the storm; or 
Voters who reasonably expect school, child care, or adult care to be canceled and will need to provide care on Election Day. 
Requesting an Absentee Ballot 
Applications are available: 
State Election Absentee Ballot Application 
Municipal Election Absentee Ballot Application 
Federal Post Card Application (FPCA)  for eligible military and overseas voters 
In person  at the City Clerk’s Office, Monday–Thursday, 7:00 AM–5:00 PM 
By mail , by contacting our office, and requesting an application 
Completed applications may be submitted by: 
Mail: 
City Clerk’s Office 
51 North Park Street 
Lebanon, NH 03766 
Email:  Submit a scanned or photographed signed application through our secure  contact portal . 
Fax:  603-874-1269 
Absentee ballots are issued only to the voter and may be mailed or personally delivered to the applicant. Another person may deliver your completed application to our office, but cannot pick up your absentee ballot on your behalf. 
Completing Your Absentee Ballot 
Your absentee ballot includes instructions, an  Affidavit Envelope , and a  Return Envelope . Please carefully follow the enclosed instructions. 
Mark Your Ballot 
Vote for no more than the number of candidates indicated for each office. You may also vote for a write-in candidate where permitted. 
Complete the Affidavit Envelope 
Place your completed ballot inside the Affidavit Envelope, complete and sign the affidavit, and seal the envelope. A missing signature may result in the ballot being challenged. 
Complete the Return Envelope 
Place the sealed Affidavit Envelope inside the Return Envelope. Any voter registration or supporting documents should be placed in the Return Envelope, not inside the Affidavit Envelope. 
Returning Your Absentee Ballot 
Completed absentee ballots may be returned by mail, personally by the voter, or by an authorized delivery agent. 
By Delivery Agent 
New Hampshire law allows certain individuals to return a voter’s absentee ballot, including: 
A spouse, parent, sibling, child, grandchild, parent-in-law, child-in-law, stepparent, or stepchild 
An authorized nursing home or residential care facility administrator or staff member 
A person assisting a blind voter or voter with a disability, subject to the requirements of state law 
Delivery agents must complete the required form and provide identification or have their identity verified. See  RSA 657:17 . 
Do not leave absentee ballots in the green mail receptacle outside City Hall.  
Important Deadlines 
Day Before Election Day 
The deadline to request an absentee ballot that must be mailed to you is 12:00 PM.  
The deadline to request and return an absentee ballot in person at the City Clerk’s Office is 5:00 PM. 
Election Day 
Absentee ballots returned by mail or an authorized delivery agent must be received by the applicable deadline under New Hampshire law. Please return your ballot as early as possible to avoid delivery delays. 
For current absentee voting deadlines and requirements, visit the  New Hampshire Secretary of State’s Absentee Voting page . 
Military and Overseas Voters 
Eligible uniformed service members, their dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas may use the  Federal Post Card Application  (FPCA)  to register to vote and request an absentee ballot. 
Eligible UOCAVA voters may choose to receive their ballot by mail, email, or fax. Ballots received electronically must still be returned in accordance with the instructions provided with the ballot. 
For additional information, visit the  New Hampshire Secretary of State’s UOCAVA Voting page . 
Track Your Absentee Ballot 
Use the  New Hampshire Voter Information Lookup  to check: 
When your absentee ballot application was received 
When your ballot was sent 
When your completed ballot was received by the City Clerk’s Office
